title: ctypes buffer handles are Python ints; kernel-arg setter misclassified them
body: First run of the new ctypes OpenCL binding failed at the first clSetKernelArg with cl_int=-51 (CL_INVALID_ARG_SIZE): Context.buffer() returned the raw c_void_p int, and set_arg() matched it in the isinstance(value, int) branch, passing a 4-byte int where an 8-byte cl_mem was required. Fixed by wrapping buffers in ctypes.c_void_p at creation and branching on that type first. Lesson: any FFI helper whose handle type aliases a scalar type must tag handles at construction, or every consumer re-derives the distinction wrong.

title: Rows assumed examples/igpu_*.py proven; files did not exist anywhere in tree
body: Board rows 47990/47992 premise a PROVEN OpenCL path at examples/igpu_opencl_compute.py exit 0, but find over the whole azazael tree returned zero igpu_*.py files and no examples/ dir. Resolved by building the premise: new stdlib-ctypes binding plus both door scripts, verified exit 0 with VERDICT lines and a max|d|=1.303e-06 device-vs-Python check on 2026-11-12. Lesson: a row that says run X must first prove X exists; a missing prerequisite is a falsification of the row, not a pass.

title: CPU OpenCL device beats Arc GPU at small matvec shapes
body: Door-2 table on 2026-11-12: at 64->128/128->256/256->512 the CPU device took 0.031/0.035/0.059 ms vs GPU 0.036/0.043/0.135 ms (gpu/cpu 0.44-0.84x). Dispatch plus transfer dominates below ~512 outputs, so a fixed GPU-always policy would be a pessimization there. This is exactly the measurement HybridDense.tune exists to exploit: pin the split per shape, never assume the accelerator wins.

title: Cosine batch 15.34x on Arc with 4.58e-08 probe agreement
body: New examples/igpu_cosine_kernel.py over N=4096 D=256: pure-Python 50.01 ms vs OpenCL 3.26 ms = 15.34x, probe rows max|d|=4.58e-08 against pure-Python cosine. Row norms precomputed on host, matching how the memory store keeps them beside vectors. Exit 0 with VERDICT line on Intel Arc 140T via stdlib ctypes, no pyopencl import.

title: HybridDense delegated step/zero_grad to Dense, which has neither method
body: Measured while benchmarking HybridDense for row 47994: every gpu_pct below 1.0 raised AttributeError: 'Dense' object has no attribute 'step'. mcml.Dense carries gW/gb but only Sequential defines step and zero_grad, so HybridDense.step calling self.cpu_layer.step(lr) was unreachable-but-broken code that only runs below 100% GPU. Fixed by resetting and updating the CPU side inline with Sequential's own math. Lesson: a subclass that delegates to a sibling class must assert the sister method exists, not assume symmetry.

title: program.<kernel> access in pyopencl builds a NEW kernel every call
body: GpuDense read self.ctx.program.dense_forward/dense_backward/dense_step on every call, and pyopencl constructs a fresh kernel object on each attribute access -- warned as RepeatedKernelRetrieval but not an error. Caching via cl.Kernel(program, name) in __init__ moved the same batch benchmark from cpu 73.03 vs opencl 161.96 ms (0.45x) to cpu 73.73 vs opencl 51.24 ms (1.44x). A performance claim taken before this fix was therefore backwards, and it was corrected in the commit that fixed the cause.

title: Batch pass accumulates a SUM, so effective learning rate scaled with batch size and went nan
body: First network-evolution runs on a 256-sample batch returned val loss nan for every hidden width, while the same code at 32 samples trained to 0.24. Cause: FusedPair.backward_batch and Dense.backward accumulate over every sample in the batch, so the step direction is a summed gradient whose magnitude grows with batch size; lr 0.01 was stable at 32 and explosive at 256. Fixed by dividing the output gradient by the batch size before backward (backward is linear in gy, so this makes it a mean gradient) in both the GPU and CPU scorers. After the fix: hidden 8 -> 0.4226, 128 -> 0.2998, 256 -> 0.2280 at 40 steps. Lesson: a loop that steps once per batch must divide by the batch, or its learning rate silently depends on a hyperparameter nobody varied on purpose.

title: Flat evolution gradient was the task, not the machinery
body: First 4-generation run was FLAT: gen-1 best 0.07953 never beaten. Measured instead of breeding longer (E2R-6): hidden widths 8..256 on the original tanh-only target all scored 0.072-0.088 with no monotonic trend, and GPU and CPU losses agreed to 5 decimals at every width. So the search space had no gradient -- every topology saturated the task. Replaced the target with one carrying high-frequency and multiplicative terms and 256 train samples, where capacity measurably pays, and the same 5-generation loop then improved 0.20973 -> 0.19220. The GPU/CPU agreement to 5 decimals is retained as a cross-check that the fused path trains identically.
